sources.textbook_title: Halliday & Resnick Fundamentals of Physics, 10th edition, Extended, Jearl Walker
sources.page_numbering: PDF page is the 1-based viewer page; relevant printed pages are PDF page minus 36.

units.title: Math Tools & Measurement
units.summary: Build the measurement, algebra, graphing, and trigonometry habits that every later unit uses.
units.inquiry: Measure a small object five times with a ruler. State the ruler resolution, calculate the mean and spread, and distinguish repeated-reading variation from a possible zero error. Then time several walks over the same marked distance. Plot position against time, draw a best-fit line, and explain the slope with units. Change one method to reduce uncertainty and compare the evidence.

lessons.title: SI units and dimensional reasoning
lessons.goal: Convert a measurement to SI units and check whether an equation has consistent dimensions.

lessons.title: Scientific notation and significant figures
lessons.goal: Report a calculation to a precision justified by its measurements.

lessons.title: Accuracy, precision, and uncertainty
lessons.goal: Describe the quality of data and judge whether an experimental result agrees with a model.

lessons.title: Algebra and a repeatable problem-solving method
lessons.goal: Rearrange a physical equation before substituting values and evaluate the result.

lessons.title: Graphing, slope, and area
lessons.goal: Extract physical meaning and correct units from the slope or area of a graph.

lessons.title: Trigonometry and vector components
lessons.goal: Resolve a vector into signed perpendicular components and reconstruct its magnitude and direction.
equations: Aₓ = A cos θ; Aᵧ = A sin θ
Rₓ = Aₓ + Bₓ; Rᵧ = Aᵧ + Bᵧ

units.title: Motion
units.summary: Describe one-dimensional motion with words, vectors, graphs, and constant-acceleration equations.
units.inquiry: Record a toy cart or walking motion against a measured background. Use several equally spaced times to build a position-time table, then estimate interval velocities. Identify a nearly uniform segment and an accelerating segment. Explain the effect of video frame rate, camera angle, and position resolution on the conclusion. Never infer constant acceleration from only two positions.

lessons.title: Position, displacement, distance, and average velocity
lessons.goal: Distinguish the length of a path from a signed change in position.

lessons.title: Instantaneous velocity and interpreting position graphs
lessons.goal: Use a local graph slope to infer velocity and recognize a turning point.
equations: v at an instant ≈ slope of tangent to x-t graph

lessons.title: Acceleration and the signs of motion
lessons.goal: Calculate acceleration and decide whether speed increases or decreases.

lessons.title: Constant-acceleration equations and their derivation
lessons.goal: Choose and apply a kinematic equation under the constant-acceleration assumption.

lessons.title: Signed graph areas and multi-stage trips
lessons.goal: Calculate displacement and distance separately from a velocity-time graph.
equations: Δx = signed area under v-t graph
Δv = signed area under a-t graph

units.title: Projectiles
units.summary: Separate horizontal and vertical motion, then reconnect them through a shared flight time.
units.inquiry: Use a soft ball rolling off a low surface, with an adult or teacher supervising the setup. Predict its landing distance from height and horizontal launch speed. Record several trials and compare with the no-drag model. Discuss uncertainty in the launch point and speed. An alternative is to collect simulated data from the trajectory explorer and clearly label it as model data, not an experiment.

lessons.title: Vertical motion and free fall
lessons.goal: Solve upward and downward motion with a consistent sign convention.

lessons.title: Independent components and horizontal launches
lessons.goal: Find flight time vertically and range horizontally for a horizontal launch.
equations: for horizontal launch from height h: t = √(2h/g)

lessons.title: Angled launches and equal-height range
lessons.goal: Resolve an angled launch and identify when the shortcut range formula applies.
equations: v₀ₓ = v₀ cos θ; v₀ᵧ = v₀ sin θ

lessons.title: Unequal launch and landing heights
lessons.goal: Solve the vertical quadratic and select the physical flight time.

lessons.title: Velocity during flight and evaluating the model
lessons.goal: Reconstruct the velocity vector at a chosen time and explain ideal-model limitations.
equations: velocity angle: tan φ = vᵧ/vₓ  (check signs)

units.title: Forces
units.summary: Use interactions and free-body diagrams to explain motion, contact forces, friction, and apparent weight.
units.inquiry: Pull a block with a spring scale on a level surface. Record the largest force just before sliding and the force during nearly constant-speed sliding. Change the load while keeping the surfaces the same. Plot friction versus normal force and discuss the dry-friction model. Use small loads and keep hands clear of falling masses. Predict before measuring; explain a specific source of uncertainty.

lessons.title: Newton’s first and second laws
lessons.goal: Relate net force to acceleration and distinguish balanced motion from rest.

lessons.title: Free-body diagrams and interaction pairs
lessons.goal: Draw only forces acting on the chosen object and identify Newton’s third-law pairs.

lessons.title: Mass, gravity, and normal force
lessons.goal: Calculate gravitational force and determine the normal force from vertical dynamics.
equations: level surface with upward applied force: N + F_up - mg = maᵧ

lessons.title: Tension and spring forces
lessons.goal: Model an ideal rope and use Hooke’s law within a spring’s elastic range.
equations: at rest for a hanging mass: T = mg

lessons.title: Static and kinetic friction
lessons.goal: Choose the correct friction model and determine friction before assuming motion.

lessons.title: Elevators and apparent weight
lessons.goal: Predict a scale’s support force from acceleration rather than direction of travel.

units.title: 2D Forces & Simple Machines
units.summary: Resolve forces on ramps, analyze connected objects, and explain how simple machines exchange force for distance.
units.inquiry: Compare lifting a small load vertically with pulling it up a gentle ramp. Measure force and travel distance, then compare input work with the change in gravitational potential energy. Research an example of a simple machine using a publicly shared source from a local First Nation or an Indigenous-led organization. Cite the community and source, respect sharing protocols, and explain the mechanical principle without treating diverse First Peoples as one culture.

lessons.title: Angled forces and equilibrium
lessons.goal: Apply Newton’s second law independently along two axes.
equations: Fₓ = F cos θ; Fᵧ = F sin θ
level floor, aᵧ = 0, upward pull: N = mg - F sin θ

lessons.title: Inclined planes without friction
lessons.goal: Choose axes along a ramp and resolve gravity relative to those axes.
equations: N = mg cos θ  (no other perpendicular forces)

lessons.title: Friction on ramps and the threshold of slipping
lessons.goal: Decide whether a block remains at rest and calculate acceleration after sliding begins.
equations: rest possible if mg sin θ ≤ μₛmg cos θ
sliding down: a = g(sin θ - μₖ cos θ)

lessons.title: Connected masses and ideal pulleys
lessons.goal: Write one equation per body and use the rope constraint to solve a system.

lessons.title: Simple machines, mechanical advantage, and levers
lessons.goal: Relate force advantage to travel distance and use torque balance for an ideal lever.
equations: ideal lever: F_in r_in = F_out r_out

units.title: Energy & Thermal Physics
units.summary: Track work and energy in a defined system, calculate power and efficiency, and apply energy conservation to heating.
units.inquiry: Design an insulated warm-water/cool-water mixing investigation. Measure masses and initial temperatures, predict equilibrium temperature, then measure it. Account for the cup and thermometer if their heat capacities matter. Compare the prediction and data, identify heat leakage and timing limitations, and propose improvements. Use warm rather than boiling water. Relate insulation choices to an energy-efficient structure using a properly attributed, publicly shared community source.

lessons.title: Work and force-displacement graphs
lessons.goal: Determine the sign and magnitude of work, including work by a changing force.
equations: W = signed area under F_parallel-versus-position graph

lessons.title: Kinetic energy and the work-energy theorem
lessons.goal: Use net work to calculate a change in speed without first finding time.

lessons.title: Potential energy and conservative forces
lessons.goal: Choose a potential-energy reference and calculate gravitational or spring energy changes.

lessons.title: Conservation of energy with and without friction
lessons.goal: Choose a system boundary and include thermal energy when mechanical energy decreases.
equations: frictionless isolated model: K_i + U_i = K_f + U_f
with thermal increase: K_i + U_i + W_ext = K_f + U_f + ΔE_th

lessons.title: Power and efficiency
lessons.goal: Distinguish energy from its transfer rate and calculate useful output.

lessons.title: Temperature, heat, and specific heat capacity
lessons.goal: Calculate energy transfer for a temperature change without a phase change.

lessons.title: Thermal equilibrium and calorimetry
lessons.goal: Apply energy conservation to objects reaching a shared final temperature.
equations: ΣQ = 0  (insulated, no work or phase change)

units.title: Electricity
units.summary: Use charge and energy conservation to solve DC circuits, real batteries, and electrical power problems.
units.inquiry: With a teacher-approved low-voltage battery circuit, measure current through and voltage across a resistor at several settings. Plot V versus I and compare the slope with resistance. Repeat with series and parallel combinations and test junction and loop rules within uncertainty. Use only low-voltage classroom equipment; never investigate a wall outlet. Connect an ammeter in series and a voltmeter across the component.

lessons.title: Charge, current, voltage, and resistance
lessons.goal: Explain each circuit quantity and connect its definition to its unit.

lessons.title: Ohm’s law and electrical measurements
lessons.goal: Identify an ohmic component and infer resistance from a graph or circuit measurements.
equations: I = slope of I-versus-V graph × V for a line through origin

lessons.title: Series circuits
lessons.goal: Find equivalent resistance and distribute voltage along one unbranched current path.

lessons.title: Parallel circuits and mixed networks
lessons.goal: Recognize common nodes, find branch currents, and simplify a mixed circuit in stages.
equations: for two branches: R_eq = R₁R₂/(R₁ + R₂)

lessons.title: Kirchhoff’s junction and loop rules
lessons.goal: Write current and voltage equations with a consistent sign convention.

lessons.title: EMF, internal resistance, and terminal voltage
lessons.goal: Distinguish a battery’s energy-per-charge supply from the voltage delivered under load.

lessons.title: Electrical power, energy, and transmission
lessons.goal: Calculate electrical energy and explain why high-voltage transmission reduces resistive loss.
equations: for a resistor: P = I²R = V²/R

units.title: Waves & Sound
units.summary: Describe mechanical waves, predict interference and resonance, and connect wave properties to sound.
units.inquiry: Observe a pulse on a gently stretched rope or use the wave explorer. Track the pulse and one marked point of the medium separately. Then compare standing-wave patterns in an ideal string and an air column. For a low-volume sound investigation, collect resonance or beat data and report room conditions, length measurement, and sound-speed assumptions. Discuss environmental noise and the limits of loudness comparisons without calibrated instruments.

lessons.title: Generating waves: energy and medium motion
lessons.goal: Distinguish transverse and longitudinal waves and separate wave travel from particle motion.
equations: wavefront = points at the same phase

lessons.title: Amplitude, wavelength, frequency, period, and speed
lessons.goal: Read wave properties from spatial and time graphs and use v = fλ.

lessons.title: Reflection, refraction, transmission, and diffraction
lessons.goal: Predict wave behavior at a boundary or opening and state which quantities change.
equations: at a stationary boundary: f₁ = f₂

lessons.title: Superposition and interference
lessons.goal: Add simultaneous displacements and relate path difference to reinforcement or cancellation.

lessons.title: Standing waves, resonance, and string harmonics
lessons.goal: Locate nodes and antinodes and determine the allowed frequencies of a fixed-end string.

lessons.title: Sound speed, pitch, intensity, and sound level
lessons.goal: Connect frequency to pitch, intensity to sound level, and travel time to distance.
equations: sound speed in air at 20 °C: v ≈ 343 m/s
I = P/A; point source I = P/(4πr²)

lessons.title: Air-column resonance and beats
lessons.goal: Distinguish open and closed pipe harmonics and calculate beat frequency.

lessons.title: Doppler shifts and sonic booms
lessons.goal: Predict frequency changes from relative motion and distinguish a sonic boom from ordinary Doppler shift.
equations: source approaches stationary observer: f_obs = f v/(v - v_s)
source recedes: f_obs = f v/(v + v_s)
observer approaches stationary source: f_obs = f(v + v_o)/v
